text:
maria: alerting eng-oncall, seeing an uptick in KV cache mismatch errors in prod-us-west around 10:03 UTC. Users reporting fragments of other sessions in completions. metrics: kv_seq_mismatch +400% and continuous-batching latency spike.

incident-bot: Incident raised (INC-2026-1003). Severity S2. Pager: @maria. Runbook: paging -> eng-oncall.

ajay: i'm on it. quick check: batching windows jumped for some GPUs after the 09:55 deploy. continuous-batcher shows many small windows but high concurrency; eviction rate fell off at 10:01.

kevin: log sample (from gpu-u1-02):
```
[10:02:58] WARN kv_cache: page_reuse_conflict: page_id=0x7f9a3 seq_expected=4521 seq_observed=4470 origin_pool=pool-A
[10:03:01] ERROR batch: emitted_response contains stray_kv_token(s) count=1 request_id=req-4231
```
This looks like paged segments being handed out with stale seq pointers.

sophie: customer-facing impact? @customer-success

customer-success: two tenants reported visible cross-session contamination: "FinEdge" and "MacroShop". Both throttled traffic and opened support tickets. FinEdge reported a failed compliance audit draft being corrupted.

maria: escalate to severity S1 if customer impact expands. For now, we'll follow containment steps.

ajay: immediate mitigation options: (A) disable paged reuse on affected pools, (B) shrink batch delay to minimize page lifetime in-flight, (C) cordon noisy nodes and failover. Disabling reuse is fastest.

ops-bot: quick command to toggle per-pool: `infractl pool set prod-us-west pool=pool-A paged_reuse_enabled=false`

maria: do the toggle. also reduce continuous batch delay: `infractl pool set prod-us-west pool=pool-A max_batch_delay_ms=2`

ops-bot: Applying change to pool-A nodes (gpu-u1-01..gpu-u1-04) ...
ops-bot: gpu-u1-01 ok. gpu-u1-02 ok. gpu-u1-03 ok. gpu-u1-04 ok. Changes in effect at 10:12 UTC.

kevin: after toggle, kv_seq_mismatch dropped to ~1.2x baseline and stray token reports fell. However, tail latency rose ~18% on pool-A.

sophie: customers confirming partial recovery?

customer-success: FinEdge confirms contamination stopped after 10:15 and are running a replay. MacroShop still seeing sporadic artefacts on low traffic tests but much reduced.

maria: good. keep reuse off. we need root cause: i want heap/paged-index snapshots from the moment of error and the deploy that changed window-size.

ajay: collecting dumps now. also noticed the deploy included a parallel migration that adjusted page_size and window_size simultaneously. suspect a race where page ownership and metadata update weren't atomic.

kevin: on analysis: allocator code allowed in-place update of page header metadata while page references could be handed to batches — no write barrier. if a migration resized windows during active traffic, some batches got pointers to pages that had been logically retyped. hence wrong seq offsets.

maria: can we craft a small in-prod fix that is safe?

kevin: short-term hotfix: ensure page header carries a generation tag `gen_id` and validate gen_id at refill time; if mismatch, treat as miss and never reuse. cheap and safe. I'll push patch to the runtime hotfix branch.

ajay: propose also adding a temporary admission control to throttle concurrent page migrations: `max_concurrent_page_migrations=1` for prod-us-west. That reduces chance of overlapping changes.

ops-bot: Applying `max_concurrent_page_migrations=1` to prod-us-west pools ... done at 10:28 UTC.

night-oncall: 10:30 handoff: i'll monitor alerts through 03:00 local. If we see seq-drift > 0.5 for 5m, i'll escalate back to S1 and wake team.

kevin: pushed `hotfix/kv-gen-guard` branch. plan: roll to a ~5% canary on prod-us-west then ramp if stable. includes added gen_id check and extra logging.

ops-bot: Starting canary rollout of hotfix/kv-gen-guard -> prod-us-west pool-A (5% nodes) at 10:36 UTC. Health checks: ok.

maria: excellent. keep reuse disabled until hotfix verified. also open a support note for the affected customers explaining mitigation and timeline.

customer-success: sent interim notes to FinEdge and MacroShop. They requested a follow-up postmortem and ask whether this was caused by the 09:55 deploy. We confirmed the deploy changed page/window params.

ajay: next actions (short): (1) complete canary and ramp hotfix if no seq-mismatch regression (2) add unit/integration tests that flip window_size under load in staging (3) add alert for any page gen mismatch occurrences > 0.1% of requests.

kevin: longer-term RCA: make page metadata updates atomic and include provenance metadata so reused pages are traceable. I'll own the allocator fix PR and test harness.

maria: i'll own the postmortem and customer comms. assign kevin for code fix, ajay for rollout coordination, and sophie for downstream docs and runbook updates.

ops-bot: Canary reached 100% on pool-A at 10:49 UTC. All checks green. gen_mismatch events = 0 in last 10m.

incident-bot: INC-2026-1003 mitigated at 10:55 UTC. Severity downgraded to S3 pending RCA.

maria: timeline for notes: detection 10:03, mitigation toggle 10:12, temporary migration throttle 10:28, hotfix canary start 10:36, full roll 10:49, mitigated 10:55. Estimated affected traffic: ~0.8% of global requests; impacted tenants: 7 reported, 2 confirmed visible contamination.

sophie: action items to close: add runbook snippet for 'paged reuse loss' (who toggles flags, which metrics to check), add postmortem draft, schedule cross-team postmortem review.

kevin: one more thing: adding a small diagnostic header to the allocator responses `X-PagedGen: <gen_id>` so we can trace if any leakage happens again. Will include in PR.

maria: thanks everyone. I'll start the postmortem template and ping for reviews.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1003 archived to /incidents/2026/1003 after mitigation.
